correctness.rationale: The proof partitions codewords into adjacent-one loops and separated-one pairs. Each uses respectively one or two distinct singleton-one deletion outputs, yielding ell+2e<=n-1. Consecutive loop positions are forbidden by an explicit common output obtained by deleting zeros, so ell<=ceil((n-1)/2). These inequalities give the claimed upper bound. Explicit even adjacent pairs and period-four separated pairs attain it, with all singleton and double-one descendants separated by parity, gap, and nonoverlapping first-one positions. The corner n=2 and all larger integers are included. A separate runnable checker confirms direct disjointness n=2..96 and exact optimum n=2..8. Finite checks supplement, not replace, the proof.

value.rationale: Single deletion is the foundational synchronization-error channel; fixing Hamming weight two isolates a natural and useful constant-composition subproblem whose exact cardinality is not supplied by ordinary unrestricted deletion-code optima. The theorem solves this infinite extremal family uniformly, identifies the additional adjacent-loop obstruction missed by basic shadow counting, and provides a regular explicit optimal code. Its 3n/4-scale answer and two-type mechanism are substantive structural information rather than a tabular finite increment.
